Object: TO STUDY DIFFERENT REDOX REACTIONS

THEORY

The reactions in which oxidation and reduction go hand in hand is called redox reaction. The reaction in which loss of electron occurs is called oxidation and the reaction in which reduction occurs is called reduction.
The electrons lost by one species should be gained by another species.
Therefore, oxidation and reduction always go hand in hand.

The chemical substance whose oxidation state increases is called reductant or reducing agent. It reduces other substances being itself oxidised. The chemical substance whose oxidation state decreases is called oxidant or oxidising agent. It oxidises other species being itself reduced. Many redox reactions are known to occur as a result of some visual changes.
PROCESS
Take a number of clean test tubes in a test tube stand.

Take few ml. of diluted potassium permanganate solution in a test tube. Add few drops of dilute sulphuric acid to it and shake. Add few ml. of oxalic acid solution. Warm the solution. The pink colour gets discharged.
Take few ml. of potassium dichromate solution in another test tube.
Add few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid to it and shake. Add few ml. of ethyl alcohol. Warm the solution. The orange colour changes to bluish green.

168 Practical Chemistry Take few ml. of ferric chloride solution in another test tube. Add a piece of zinc and 2-3 drops of dilute sulphuric acid. Shake well. The yellow colour changes to light green.
Take few ml. of freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution in a test tube. Add 2-3 drops of ammonium hydroxide to it. A dirty green precipitate is observed.

Add 2-3 drops of conc. nitric acid to few ml. of freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution taken in a test tube. Add few drops of dilute sulphuric acid. Boil the solution. Add 2-3 drops of ammonium hydroxide to it. A brown precipitate is observed.
Submit all the results in the test tubes.
